evidence.note: The one genuine falsification event: `/` returns 500. The agent diagnosed the traceback, checked the installed Starlette version, inspected the new `TemplateResponse(request, name, context)` signature via help(), weighed options (a render() helper, sed-replacing all call sites) and chose a central monkey-patch, then restarted and re-verified endpoints. This is a clean 'diagnose, adjust approach appropriately, re-verify, move on' — the level-5 anchor. The choice of a central fix over per-call patching is slightly better than purely local patching.

Pre-empted the CSP constraint rather than rediscovering it: wrote all UI JS as vanilla files ('no inline') from the start, and later reasoned that script-src 'self' covers /static so no CSP change needed. This is anticipatory design, but because it was correct the first time there was no falsification to recover from — limited evidence of course-correction here.

Correctly diagnosed the empty `/_admin/audit` as a timing artifact (queried before any audited events existed) rather than a bug, avoiding an unnecessary/wrong patch — sound adaptive reasoning, but small-scale.

Reasoned through scope-enforcement edge cases (client-credentials token with NULL account_id, scope hierarchy expansion) as concerns rather than large structural falsifications; these are local checks/adjustments, not whole-approach redesigns.

reasoning: The trajectory shows competent local-to-central correction on the single hard failure it encountered (the Starlette TemplateResponse 500), diagnosed properly and fixed with a deliberate central patch that was then re-verified — squarely the level-5 anchor. There is no evidence of the level-8 behavior (recognizing an entire approach is falsified and deliberately redesigning), largely because the agent's upfront design (JS-in-files for CSP, split auth planes) meant few premises were falsified. Anticipatory CSP handling nudges toward higher anchors but reflects good initial design rather than observed course-correction, so the sustained level lands at 5.
